title: CuTe DSL Compilation Options Overview
critical_patterns: Development: Use -O0 for fast compile times and enable debugging
Production: Use -O3 for maximum performance and disable debugging
Benchmarking: Enable profiling for accurate timing
Debugging Performance: Dump code and keep PTX for analysis
constraints: Most options are read at import time
Target correct architecture for GPU compatibility
Use subprocess to change options after import
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL offers a range of compilation options to optimize GPU kernel development, focusing on environment variables to control settings like optimization levels, debug modes, target architectures, and compiler flags. Key concepts include setting environment variables before importing the cutlass module to ensure they take effect, with options such as CUTLASS_OPT_LEVEL for optimization (ranging from 0 for no optimization to 3 for aggressive optimization), CUTLASS_DEBUG for enabling or disabling debug symbols, and CUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS for specifying target GPU architectures. Practical patterns include using -O0 and enabling debugging for development to facilitate fast iteration and error checking, while production environments should use -O3 for performance and disable debugging to reduce overhead. Benchmarking setups should enable profiling to gather accurate performance metrics. Developers should be cautious to set options before importing cutlass as changes made post-import won't affect compilation. Additionally, targeting the correct architecture is crucial for ensuring compatibility and performance. Best practices emphasize documenting configurations and using verbose modes during debugging to gain insights into the compilation process. The document also covers advanced options like controlling verbosity with CUTLASS_VERBOSE, saving generated code with CUTLASS_DUMP_CODE, and keeping PTX files for low-level analysis. For runtime option changes, using subprocesses is recommended to apply new settings effectively. Overall, understanding and utilizing these options can significantly impact the efficiency and effectiveness of GPU kernel development with CuTe DSL.
